$comment: Public allowlist for the platform graph. Only what is listed here can reach the site. Registry rows not mapped under `services` are dropped. Never put hostnames, IPs, ports, paths or tailnet names here.

card.what: Thin client. All code, agents and services run on the home server; the laptop only connects.
card.why: One machine holds state, secrets and long-running agents; clients stay disposable.
card.decision: Development moved fully to the server; the laptop is a terminal and a browser.

card.what: 8 keys on the laptop: one per project plus the main agent and a session list.
card.why: One press reattaches to the right agent session instead of remembering where work stopped.
card.decision: Each key opens SSH into the server and attaches to a per-project tmux session (created if missing).

card.what: An old tablet (iOS 12) showing the status board: projects, running agents, who needs a human.
card.why: Agents that wait for permission are visible without opening a terminal.
card.decision: ES5-only front end for Safari 12; polls the board every 10 s. The device cannot run Tailscale, so it is the one LAN exception.

card.what: Tailscale network: every device and service talks over it, with HTTPS certificates inside the tailnet.
card.why: Nothing on the server is reachable from the internet.
card.decision: Policy S2: no Funnel, no router port-forwarding. Services get their own tailnet node via a sidecar container.

card.what: A single firewall rule lets exactly one device (the tablet) reach the status board over the home LAN.
card.why: The tablet cannot join the tailnet.
card.decision: An automated exposure check flagged the board listening on all interfaces → documented exception with date and owner → firewall narrowed from the whole subnet to one device.

card.what: One long-lived tmux session per project, each running Claude Code in that project's folder.
card.why: Agents survive disconnects; any client can reattach.
card.decision: Sessions are named per project so the board and the Stream Deck find the same session.

card.what: Claude Code skill: intent → matching procedure → plan → verifier → execute → verifier → log.
card.why: Infrastructure changes follow a written procedure instead of improvisation.
card.decision: No procedure for an intent → do it step by step with the owner, then draft a new procedure. Step 0 is a wiki freshness check.

card.what: A separate subagent with a fresh context and read-only tools. Before: GO/STOP on the plan. After: PASS/FAIL from checks.
card.why: The executor should not grade its own work. A check that could not run counts as FAIL.
card.decision: A STOP overrides the executor. It never prints or expands secrets — a rule added after an API key surfaced in its output during a migration (the key was rotated).

card.what: 6 hook events (session start/end, prompt submit, stop, notification, tool use) append one line each to a local event log.
card.why: The board knows which agent is working, waiting for permission or idle.
card.decision: Only metadata is logged: event, short session id, project, tool name. Never prompt text or file contents.

card.what: agent-wiki: service registry, permissions (agent alone / asks / human only), security policies S1–S10, secrets rules.
card.why: Agents and the owner read the same rules; every change is a reviewed diff.
card.decision: Exceptions are recorded with date, reason and owner, and mirrored in a machine-readable file the checks honour.

card.what: Step-by-step procedures with inputs, preconditions, steps marked ASK, checks, rollback and done criteria.
card.why: Repeatable changes; the verifier checks against preconditions, not against intent.
card.decision: Reality differs from the procedure → the executor proposes a wiki diff; the owner approves; the next run uses it.

card.what: 6 shell checks: container health, HTTPS inside the tailnet, compose policy, live exposure, secrets in git, image CVEs.
card.why: "Done" is a check that passes, not a sentence.
card.decision: Exit 0 = PASS, 1 = FAIL, 2 = WARN. A check that let a problem through gets a new check, not a new paragraph.

card.what: Projects and a session log. Every working session leaves a short entry; an evening job collects the day.
card.why: Sessions do not see each other; the log is the bridge.
card.decision: What & why lives in Notion, how & by which rules lives in git. One fact in one place.

card.what: Agents commit on branches and open pull requests.
card.why: Every change is reviewable and reversible.
card.decision: Merging is human-only, as are sudo, secret values and admin consoles.

card.what: One JSON line per routed request: decision, route, latency, config hash. Built from an allow-list of fields.
card.why: Metrics and evals without storing anyone's text.
card.decision: A canary test plants a marker in every free-text field and fails if it reaches the log (ADR-005).

card.what: One project, three parts: a PWA console, an OpenAI-compatible API and a local model runtime on the same CPU-only box.
card.why: Keep sensitive requests on my own hardware and send the rest to the cheapest cloud model that can handle them.
card.decision: Only the console is reachable, and only inside the tailnet; the API binds to loopback; model and policy changes go through preregistered evals.

card.what: Interview trainer: Python in the browser (Pyodide), behavioral and system-design practice, a 14-day plan.
card.why: Built for my own interview preparation.
card.decision: Own tailnet node through a Tailscale sidecar, tailnet-only; moved there with the service-own-address procedure (verifier GO → PASS).

card.what: Next.js PWA chat console for jev in a hardened container (read-only, all capabilities dropped).
card.why: Use the router from phone and laptop without exposing the API.
card.decision: Served only inside the tailnet; API keys stay server-side; history stays on the device (ADR-013).

card.what: OpenAI-compatible server for the jev router: rules → local classifier → policy → local or cloud executor.
card.why: Any OpenAI-shaped client can use privacy-aware routing.
card.decision: Refuses to bind anything but loopback; sensitive requests never leave the machine (ADR-005, ADR-011).

card.what: FastAPI board: projects from Notion, agent sessions from hook events, system load; can launch an agent per project.
card.why: See at a glance which agent is working and which one waits for me.
card.decision: Launch takes its prompt from Notion, never from text typed on the tablet. Sensitive projects are scrubbed to ID and status.

card.what: Postgres for a production-shaped Express 5 + Prisma service used to practise live coding with agents.
card.why: Practice on something with real constraints, not a toy.
card.decision: Local only, bound to loopback; container hardening by default.

card.what: Mobile app (Expo) for a family sleep routine with a Python calculation core.
card.why: Real users at home; a design system and accessibility from day one.
card.decision: Code only, not deployed yet; a node name is reserved for it.

card.what: Local model runtime on a CPU-only box; one 7B model kept loaded and warmed up at start.
card.why: Classify and answer sensitive requests without the cloud.
card.decision: qwen2.5:7b stayed after a preregistered comparison: the 9B candidate timed out on 13 of 48 calls (ADR-009).
